meta.title: R.Vittenberg — Full-Stack Development
meta.description: Independent full-stack developer building complete web products from architecture and interface to backend, integrations, deployment, and long-term support.

hero.title: I build complete digital products — from the first idea and interface to backend, integrations, deployment, and everything that comes after.

about.title: Who I am
about.body: I'm an independent full-stack developer focused on building complete web products rather than isolated pieces of software. I work across the entire development process: understanding the idea, planning the architecture, designing the interface, building the frontend and backend, connecting external services, working with databases, deploying the application, and supporting it after launch. I prefer taking responsibility for the whole result. If a project needs something outside the initial brief, I would rather solve it than leave the client to figure it out alone.

services.ul1: Full-stack web development — complete products built from the ground up.
services.ul2: Frontend development with React and Next.js, including responsive interfaces, animation, and complex client-side interactions.
services.ul3: Backend development with Django, REST APIs, authentication, business logic, and database-driven systems.
services.ul4: E-commerce, booking systems, dashboards, CRMs, SaaS products, and custom business applications.
services.ul5: Third-party integrations — payments, messaging, external APIs, authentication providers, analytics, and other services.
services.ul6: Deployment and production setup — servers, databases, domains, SSL, environment configuration, monitoring, and maintenance.

about.locationsBody: I work remotely with clients and teams regardless of where they are located. The process is direct: you talk to the person actually building the product. There is no unnecessary layer between the client and development.

pricing.li1: Every project is different, so I prefer estimating from the actual brief rather than selling artificial packages.
pricing.li2: Small fixes, integrations, and individual features can be handled as focused tasks.
pricing.li3: Larger products are planned in stages so that the client always understands what is being built and why.
pricing.li4: The goal is not to make the cheapest possible version. It is to build something that can actually be used, maintained, and developed further.

about.contactBody: The best way to reach me is by email. I keep communication direct and practical, and I'm happy to discuss an idea even when it is still only an idea.

reel.body: A product rarely ends at the interface. Someone has to think about the data, business logic, authentication, integrations, deployment, edge cases, security, and what happens six months after launch. That is the part of development I take seriously. I prefer to stay involved until the result is actually working.

featured.title: Selected Work
featured.disclaimer: Selected projects and products I have designed, developed, or worked on. Some professional work cannot be shown publicly because of confidentiality agreements.

overview.title: A digital experience for a nightlife venue.
overview.body: Daerdree Bar & Timeclub required more than a conventional business website. The goal was to create a digital presence that communicated the atmosphere of the venue while making practical things such as events, information, and reservations easy to access.

sections.title: The interface carries the atmosphere.
sections.body: The visual direction uses large typography, motion, contrast, and carefully controlled transitions to make the website feel connected to the physical venue rather than looking like a generic hospitality template.

sections.title: Reservations without unnecessary steps.
sections.body: The booking experience was designed around a short, understandable flow, with the important information presented at the moment it is needed.

sections.title: One system for the whole venue.
sections.body: Venue information, events, menus, and reservations are brought together in one responsive interface designed to work equally well on desktop and mobile.

overview.title: A website for a software company that needed to demonstrate its technical character.
overview.body: The purpose was not simply to present a list of services. The website itself had to communicate speed, precision, engineering, and attention to detail.

sections.title: The website demonstrates the product.
sections.body: Motion, interaction, and 3D elements were used as part of the experience rather than as decoration. The interface itself becomes evidence of the team's capabilities.

sections.title: Projects instead of empty promises.
sections.body: Work is presented around problems, decisions, and implementation so that a potential client can understand what was actually built.

sections.title: Small details matter.
sections.body: Typography, spacing, transitions, responsiveness, and performance were treated as part of the engineering rather than something added at the end.

spatial_fusion.name: Careyourpet (PetVet)
spatial_fusion.tags: veterinary CRM • SaaS • PostgreSQL • web • mobile

overview.title: A working CRM for veterinary clinics.
overview.body: Careyourpet is a veterinary CRM concept designed around the daily work of clinics: patients, owners, appointments, medical history, prescriptions, and vaccination records.

sections.title: One patient, one complete record.
sections.body: The system brings medical history, visits, prescriptions, and vaccination information into a unified patient record so that important information is available when it is needed.

sections.title: Software built around real work.
sections.body: Search, scheduling, records, and common actions were designed to minimize unnecessary navigation and keep staff focused on the patient.

sections.title: Functional without feeling clinical.
sections.body: The interface balances information density with a clear visual hierarchy so that the product remains approachable while handling complex data.

overview.title: A complete online retail experience.
overview.body: El-Imperia is an e-commerce project built around product discovery, catalog management, purchasing, and a straightforward customer journey.

sections.title: Products are easy to find.
sections.body: Categories, product pages, filtering, and visual hierarchy are organized around helping customers reach the right product quickly.

sections.title: A simple path to purchase.
sections.body: The purchasing flow is intentionally focused: the customer should understand what they are buying, provide the required information, and complete the order without unnecessary friction.

sections.title: Built as a real application.
sections.body: The store is not just a collection of static pages. It is a data-driven product designed to support catalog information, customer interactions, and future expansion.

spaace.name: Proffmusic.shop
spaace.tags: audio marketplace • music • e-commerce • digital assets

overview.title: A marketplace for professional audio assets.
overview.body: Proffmusic is an e-commerce concept for professional audio content such as samples, loops, and stems. The experience had to support discovery, previews, licensing, purchasing, and digital delivery.

sections.title: Listen before you buy.
sections.body: Audio previews are integrated into the browsing experience so users can evaluate assets without repeatedly leaving the catalog.

sections.title: Digital products need a different checkout.
sections.body: The purchase flow accounts for licensing and digital delivery while keeping the number of steps understandable.

sections.title: The interface belongs to the product.
sections.body: Visual language, typography, audio-related interaction, and layout work together to create a product that feels intended for producers rather than adapted from a generic store.

synthetic_human.name: Webdoc.life AI
synthetic_human.tags: healthtech • AI • laboratory reports • SaaS • Next.js

overview.title: Making laboratory reports easier to understand.
overview.body: Webdoc.life is an AI-powered product concept that processes laboratory test results and presents their meaning in understandable language. The product combines structured data, interpretation, user profiles, and history.

sections.title: Numbers need context.
sections.body: The system is designed to explain laboratory indicators, reference ranges, deviations, and terminology instead of simply returning a collection of unexplained values.

sections.title: History makes information useful.
sections.body: Results can be associated with user profiles and viewed over time, making changes and trends easier to understand.

sections.title: Sensitive data requires careful engineering.
sections.body: Projects dealing with personal and health-related information require particular attention to access control, data handling, confidentiality, and responsible product design.

overview.title: A digital experience for an eco-resort.
overview.body: GardenHouse is a hospitality concept built around nature, accommodation, seasonal stays, and booking. The website was designed to communicate the atmosphere of the place before the visitor ever arrives.

sections.title: The interface should feel like the place.
sections.body: Organic shapes, restrained motion, photography, and generous spacing create a quieter experience appropriate for a nature-focused property.

sections.title: Different rooms, different experiences.
sections.body: Accommodation options are presented as individual experiences rather than simply a list of room specifications.

sections.title: Planning a stay should be simple.
sections.body: Availability, accommodation information, rates, and booking actions are organized into a clear path from discovery to reservation.

agios.name: Taverna Agios Epiktitos
agios.tags: Cypriot cuisine • restaurant • menu • booking • web

overview.title: A website for a traditional Cypriot taverna.
overview.body: The project combines the identity of a family restaurant with practical digital functions: menu presentation, events, information, and table reservations.

sections.title: The website starts with the place itself.
sections.body: The visual direction was built around the story and atmosphere of the taverna instead of using a generic restaurant template.

sections.title: A real menu, not a photograph of one.
sections.body: Menu content is structured so that visitors can browse categories and dishes comfortably on both desktop and mobile devices.

sections.title: Bookings reach the people who need them.
sections.body: The reservation flow is connected to the owners' Telegram workflow so that incoming bookings do not disappear into an isolated contact form.

overview.title: Complex financial information, made readable.
overview.body: Walmgres is an investment platform concept where portfolio information, analytics, performance, and risk data need to remain understandable without sacrificing depth.

sections.title: Clarity comes first.
sections.body: The interface establishes a clear hierarchy between primary financial information, secondary metrics, and supporting data.

sections.title: Data has to remain usable.
sections.body: Portfolio breakdowns, performance information, and risk indicators are represented through focused visualizations designed around actual decision-making.

sections.title: Motion should explain, not distract.
sections.body: Transitions are used to communicate changes of state and guide attention rather than simply decorate the interface.

leondiana.name: Leondiana
leondiana.tags: boutique hotel • Larnaca • booking • admin panel • web

overview.title: A hotel website backed by a real management system.
overview.body: Leondiana is a boutique hotel project in Larnaca, Cyprus. The product combines a visual guest-facing website with a functional backend and administration panel for managing rooms, bookings, content, promotions, and media.

sections.title: The guest sees the simple part.
sections.body: The public website presents the hotel, rooms, gallery, location, and booking flow in a calm and responsive interface.

sections.title: Behind it is a working command center.
sections.body: The administration panel manages rooms, incoming reservations and their statuses, promotional codes, multilingual content, settings, and media.

sections.title: One source of truth.
sections.body: The product separates the user-facing frontend from the data-driven backend. Structured media can be reused across the homepage, gallery, and room pages without creating unnecessary duplicates.

services.metaDescription: Full-stack web development, product engineering, backend systems, integrations, deployment, and long-term technical support.

offers.webBody: I build complete web applications rather than only one layer of them. That means frontend, backend, database, authentication, business logic, integrations, deployment, and the less visible work required to make the product reliable. If you already have a design, I can turn it into a working application. If you only have an idea, I can help shape the technical solution.
offers.mobileBody: A product usually needs more than a collection of pages. I can help structure the application, define the data model, build the core workflows, connect external services, and turn an initial concept into something people can actually use. The work can start from a specification, a design, a prototype, or simply a conversation.
offers.aiBody: I work with external APIs, payment systems, messaging services, AI-powered functionality, data processing, and other integrations that make a product useful in the real world. The important part is not adding technology for its own sake, but making it solve an actual business problem.

services.perksTitle: What you receive with the work

perks.p1Title: One person who understands the whole system
perks.p1Body: You do not have to explain the same product separately to a designer, frontend developer, backend developer, and deployment engineer. I work across the stack and understand how the pieces affect each other.
perks.p2Body: I can take a project from an initial idea or specification through architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, and further development.
perks.p3Body: I prefer direct communication and understandable explanations. You should know what is being built, what has been completed, and what still needs attention.
perks.p4Body: Authentication, permissions, environment variables, sensitive information, database access, and third-party integrations are treated as engineering concerns rather than afterthoughts.
perks.p5Body: A significant part of professional development happens behind NDA. I understand that some projects, business ideas, source code, customer data, and internal processes are not mine to discuss publicly.
perks.p6Body: I do not consider the job finished when the code merely runs on my machine. The goal is a working product that can be deployed, used, maintained, and developed further.

why.aBody: When I accept a project, I take responsibility for getting it to a usable result. If something turns out to be more complicated than expected, I look for a solution rather than simply passing the problem back to the client.
why.bBody: A good interface is only one part of a product. I think about data, architecture, business logic, integrations, performance, deployment, maintenance, and what happens when the first version needs to grow.
why.cBody: Projects can change during development. Requirements can become clearer, unexpected problems can appear, and technical decisions sometimes need to be revisited. None of that changes the basic responsibility: the work needs to reach the finish line.
why.dBody: I'm not particularly interested in being a public personality. I keep a relatively low profile and prefer to spend my time building. The projects are the strongest explanation of what I can do.

quotes.aBody: You should not need to become a technical expert just to work with a developer. My job is to understand the technical side, explain the important decisions, and make sure the product keeps moving.
quotes.bBody: I would rather take on fewer projects and finish them properly than accept everything and leave unfinished work behind.
quotes.cBody: The result should be something I am comfortable putting my name behind. That means functioning software, sensible architecture, careful implementation, and responsibility for the details.

faq.q1: Can you build a project from scratch?
faq.a1: Yes. This is one of the main ways I work. We can start with an idea, specification, prototype, design, or existing business process. I can help translate it into a technical architecture and then build the product through to deployment.
faq.q2: Can you work with an existing design?
faq.a2: Yes. If the design is already prepared, I can turn it into a responsive production interface and connect it to the backend and required services. I can also point out technical problems in the design before they become expensive to fix.
faq.q3: Do you only work on the frontend?
faq.a3: No. My focus is full-stack development. I work with React and Next.js on the frontend and Django and PostgreSQL on the backend, alongside APIs, authentication, integrations, deployment, and related infrastructure.
faq.q4: What if I don't have a technical specification?
faq.a4: That is fine. Many projects start as a business idea and a conversation. I can help break the idea into features, identify the important technical questions, define an initial architecture, and turn that into an actionable development plan.
faq.a5: Yes. Confidentiality is a normal part of professional software development. I have worked with projects and information that cannot be publicly described. If a project requires an NDA or specific confidentiality requirements, those requirements are respected.
faq.q6: What about sensitive or private data?
faq.a6: Sensitive information should be handled carefully from the beginning. Access control, authentication, secrets, permissions, data exposure, and third-party services all need to be considered as part of the architecture. I do not treat client data or source code as something to share casually.
faq.q7: Will you leave after the website goes live?
faq.a7: Not necessarily. Launch is a milestone, not a natural reason to disappear. If you need fixes, improvements, new functionality, integrations, or continued technical support, we can continue working together.
faq.q8: What if something goes wrong during development?
faq.a8: Something unexpected eventually happens in almost every non-trivial project. The important part is how it is handled. I prefer to communicate the problem clearly, explain the available options, and work toward a practical solution rather than hide the issue or abandon the task.
faq.a9: Yes. I can work on individual features, bugs, integrations, API connections, forms, payment systems, performance problems, or other focused development tasks when they fit my stack and availability.
faq.q10: Why don't you show every project?
faq.a10: Because not every project belongs to me publicly. Some professional work is covered by NDA or contains private business information. I believe respecting that agreement is more important than having another item in a portfolio.

footer.tagline: Full-stack development from idea to production.
